summary_en: This study compares two ways to manage thyroid nodules that look likely to be cancerous on ultrasound: an immediate needle biopsy, which is usual care, or active monitoring with ultrasound and check-ups. The biopsy uses a small needle guided by ultrasound, usually with local anesthetic, while active monitoring includes an ultrasound and check-up every six months for two years, then less often. The main outcome is anxiety at 6 months, measured with the Anxiety-CA instrument, and the study also measures thyroid quality of life.
summary_es: Este estudio compara dos formas de manejar nódulos tiroideos que, según el ultrasonido, parecen probablemente cancerosos: una biopsia con aguja inmediata, que es la atención habitual, o el monitoreo activo con ultrasonido y consultas de control. La biopsia usa una aguja pequeña guiada por ultrasonido, generalmente con anestesia local, mientras que el monitoreo activo incluye un ultrasonido y una consulta cada seis meses durante dos años, y luego con menos frecuencia. El resultado principal es la ansiedad a los 6 meses, medida con el instrumento Anxiety-CA, y el estudio también mide la calidad de vida relacionada con la tiroides.
who_for: Adults 18 years or older who can give informed consent, or have a surrogate who can.
No symptoms from the nodule, such as trouble swallowing, or the nodule is visible or bothersome.
Nodule is 2 cm or smaller in largest diameter.
Being considered for biopsy; prior papillary thyroid cancer is allowed.
not_for: Prior thyroid cancer other than papillary thyroid cancer.
Prior neck radiation, or no thyroid gland (athyroidal).
Ultrasound signs of airway invasion, nerve involvement, or spread outside the thyroid; or a prior biopsy of the nodule.
